newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson says nonperforming assets fell in April.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson says nonperforming assets fell in April.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co said Friday nonperfomring assets fell $41 million during April to $752 million.

Ahmanson said single-family nonaccrual laons fell by $25 million to $486 million for the 14th consecutive monthly improvement. Ahmanson said single-family nonaccrual loans have declined by $202 million or 29 percent since a recent peak in February 1996. Foreclosed single-family real estate declined by $14 million in April for the seventh consecutive montly decrease, Ahmanson said.

Ahmanson said single-family loans delinquent 60 to 89 days fell $17 million to $83 million, the lowest level since October 1989. Ahmanson said it was the sixth consecutive month that the delinquencies have declined.

Charles Rinehart, chairman and chief executive of Ahmanson, said in a statement the company "has delivered significant improvement in credit costs and in indicators of future credit costs." He said the April results "again reflect our initiatives to strengthen underwriting and improve collection processes." He said a strengthening Southern California economy also contributed to the lower credit costs.
Rinehart noted that credit costs in the first quarter of 1997 fell by $26 million, or 36 percent, from the year-earlier quarter.

Ahmanson, based in Southern California, has made an offer to acquire Great Western Financial Corp, a thrift also based in Southern California. Great Western has agreed to merge with Seattle-based Washington Mutual Inc.
